input.question: For the hard-core lattice gas (independent-set model) on a countably infinite graph G=(V,E) of maximum degree Delta, with vertex fugacities {w_x} and Gibbs measures defined for nonnegative fugacities, is it true that uniqueness of the infinite-volume Gibbs measure holds whenever 0 <= w_x <= (1-epsilon)*(Delta-1)^(Delta-1)/(Delta-2)^Delta for all vertices x and some epsilon>0 (possibly even epsilon=0)?

original_paper.title: A Personal List of Unsolved Problems Concerning Lattice Gases and Antiferromagnetic Potts Models

rewritten_question: Let G = (V, E) be a countably infinite graph of maximum degree Δ, and let each vertex x carry a nonnegative fugacity w_x. In the hard-core lattice gas, equivalently the independent-set model, a configuration is an independent set A ⊆ V, meaning that no two adjacent vertices are both chosen; on a finite graph such a configuration has weight equal to the product of the fugacities over the vertices in A, and on a countably infinite graph the corresponding Gibbs measures are defined by the usual Dobrushin-Lanford-Ruelle prescription. Is it true that the infinite-volume Gibbs measure is unique whenever there exists some ε > 0 such that 0 ≤ w_x ≤ (1−ε)(Δ−1)^(Δ−1)/(Δ−2)^Δ for every vertex x? Is this perhaps still true in the borderline case ε = 0?

paper_evidence.quote: I review recent results and unsolved problems concerning the hard-core lattice gas and the q-coloring model ...

Let G = (V, E) be a finite graph, and let w = {wx}x∈V be a set of (possibly complex) fugacities. The partition function of the hard-core lattice gas (= independent-set polynomial) on G is Z(w) = X A ⊆ V A independent Y x∈A wx . (2.1)
(Recall that A ⊆ V is called an independent set if it does not contain any pair of adjacent vertices.)
When the fugacities are nonnegative, an equilibrium probability distribution on the state space 2V can be defined by µ(A) = Z(w)−1 Y x∈A wx × χ(A independent) . (2.2)
When G is countably infinite and the fugacities are nonnegative, Gibbs measures can then be defined by the usual Dobrushin–Lanford–Ruelle prescription [26].

Conjecture 2.1 For any countably infinite graph G of maximum degree ∆, the hard-core lattice gas on G has a unique Gibbs measure whenever 0 ≤ wx ≤ (1 − ǫ)× (∆−1)∆−1/(∆−2)∆ [∼ e/∆ for large ∆] for all vertices x, for some ǫ > 0. [Perhaps this is true even with ǫ = 0.]
It seems to be an open problem to prove Conjecture 2.1 even when G is a non-regular tree and the wx are all equal.
